=== Further shipping evidence, 1792–1797 ===

Additional advertisements in April and May 1792 explicitly name William Glasgow as master of the brig William for Rotterdam and return voyages; other named-master advertisements concern Oporto and Bordeaux. Surname-only arrival and cargo notices continue the William/Captain Glasgow trading sequence through 1796–1797, with probable rather than proved continuity. A February 1793 report describes departure from Bordeaux immediately before an embargo; it does not prove that the ship was captured or detained. Distinct notices name William Glasgow as master of the Jean in 1793 and 1794, including a safe arrival at Derry from London. Jean and William are different vessels, with compatible but unproved continuity of master. Several apparent advertisement/issue-date conflicts arise from the Northern Star’s printed issue ranges; the printed range and notice date should retain their separate meanings. The captain remains a compatible identification with William of Larne, supported by age, coastal locality and the inherited occupational suggestion. No advertisement names his wife or a personal Larne residence. The named master of the Jean may be the same man, but the vessel names do not prove it. The will dated 6 December 1815 remains the useful family-and-occupation test.
